messages:
Maria (CS): Heads-up: VelvetPay just escalated — identical rerank requests returning different scores after last night's rerank rollout. They provided an example where the same candidate set gets 0.78 before vs 0.31 after. Can someone triage? request_id=rv-9b7c

Tim (Support): Thanks Maria. Can you paste the exact request payload + the request_id trace and the two score dumps? Also which model/version was pinned prior vs the new one?

Maria (CS): Pasting minimal repro (sensitive fields redacted):
```json
{
  "query": "how do I dispute a charge",
  "candidates": ["docA","docB","docC","docD","docE"],
  "top_k": 5,
  "model": "rerank-v2.0",
  "client_request_id": "rv-9b7c"
}
```
Scores observed: before (v1.4): [0.78, 0.55, 0.42, 0.33, 0.10]  after (v2.0): [0.31, 0.58, 0.60, 0.12, 0.05]
Note: VelvetPay insists they sent the identical JSON. No truncation reported on their side.

DeployBot: Deployment event: rerank-v2.0 rolled to prod at 2026-03-16T01:12:08Z — rollout 100% (deployer: sasha.platform).

Devon (ML): OK — thanks. A couple immediate hypotheses: 1) model behavior changed (expected) 2) prompt/template change being applied at serving time 3) tokenization differences / whitespace normalization 4) quantization / kernel-selection causing small score drift (usually small, not flips). Can we get raw tokenization for the query + first candidate on both versions? Also what exact model artifact hash was used for v1.4 vs v2.0?

Maria (CS): Artifact hashes from customer logs: v1.4 -> hash a3f4e, v2.0 -> hash b9c0d. VelvetPay provided their side-by-side HTTP captures (they scrubbed auth). I uploaded the capture to the secure share: https://redwood.shares/velvetpay/rv-9b7c (internal access).

Alex (Infra): I pulled gateway logs for rv-9b7c. No 4xxs. BUT I did notice the upstream JSON rewriter we rolled on 2026-03-16 at 00:55 had a config tweak that injects a small prompt prefix for rerank models for context normalization. The rewriter log shows: 
```
rewrite: add_prefix=\"[NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE]\"\nrequest_id=rv-9b7c
```
That would change the model input tokens. Rolling back that rewriter change now for canary.

Sasha (Platform): Confirming — I merged a tiny platform change to add a normalization prefix to reduce tokenization variability across customers. It was intended to be semantic-noop, but I see it shipped in the same deploy bundle that bumped rerank to v2.0. Apologies, my rollout note missed coupling this with an eval.

Devon (ML): That prefix could absolutely affect rerank ordering — it changes tokens and attention patterns. Not a quantization artifact. Can we reproduce locally by adding the exact prefix and running v1.4 and v2.0? If v1.4+prefix matches v2.0 results, we'll know the rewriter prefix is the cause.

Maria (CS): Quick repro done against staging:
curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood/re-ranker 
  -d '{"query":"[NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE] how do I dispute a charge","candidates":["docA","docB","docC","docD","docE"],"model":"rerank-v1.4"}'
produces scores: [0.32,0.57,0.59,0.13,0.04] which matches the prod v2.0 ordering.

Tim (Support): Nice repro — so root cause is platform prompt prefix, not an inherent model regression. What's the mitigation plan? Customer wants a fast rollback.

Sasha (Platform): Mitigation options: 1) immediate rollback of the rewriter prefix to prod (low risk) 2) pin VelvetPay to rerank-v1.4 without prefix via tenant routing (medium effort) 3) run a targeted canary that includes prefix + regression evals (longer). I'll revert the prefix ASAP and open a rollout PR that adds regression tests to the release pipeline.

Alex (Infra): I'll coordinate a quick rollback of the rewrite rule (5m change window). Also adding a check to the gateway to prevent undocumented input prefixes from being injected without an eval flag.

Devon (ML): Post-mortem action: add a rerank regression suite that runs a 5k-sample eval whenever we change any input-normalization change or swap rerank artifacts. Also document that any platform-level input transforms must be tested for ordering stability.

Maria (CS): I told VelvetPay the cause is an unintended platform prefix. They've asked for status and a backfill report showing affected requests in the last 12 hours. I'll produce that after rollback.

Tim (Support): Assigning follow-ups: Sasha -> rollback + PR for regression gate. Alex -> add gateway guard and list of effected request_ids (search rv-*). Devon -> add eval harness job. Maria -> customer comms and backfill CSV.

Sasha (Platform): Rollback executed at 2026-03-16T01:38Z. Monitoring for errors.

Devon (ML): After rollback, retesting against VelvetPay sample on prod pinned to v2.0 (no prefix) returns original v1.4-like ordering? Please confirm.

Maria (CS): Confirmed — post-rollback prod (v2.0, no prefix) returns scores close to pre-rollout ordering for VelvetPay sample. Customer updated to say their QA checks now pass. 

Tim (Support): Closing loop: root cause = unintended platform-level input prefix that changed tokenization/attention, causing score reordering. Not a model weight regression. Recommended long-term: regression tests on input transforms, explicit release checklist item, and tenant-level pinning APIs. :white_check_mark:

Maria (CS): Thanks team — I'll send the customer report and attach the repro steps and timelines.
